title: TF module decomposition cheatsheet: VPC, IAM, EKS primitives and outputs
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a compact, opinionated cheat sheet for decomposing Terraform modules used across Redwood Private deployments. Goal: reduce accidental coupling, make upgrades safer, and provide a repeatable pattern for VPC / IAM / Kubernetes primitives (EKS/GKE/AKS). This is intentionally pragmatic — not a full PRD. Use as reference for module authors and reviewers.

Principles (short):
- Single responsibility: each module should own one real-world primitive (network, iam, cluster, node-pool).
- Inputs are configuration, outputs are contracts. Avoid implicit global state.
- Keep low-level modules composable; higher-level stacks assemble them.
- Backwards-compatible output surface is critical for safe rollouts. Add outputs, deprecate slowly.
- Modules should be idempotent and cheap to plan (avoid enumerating very large lists in locals).
- Explicit resource naming: allow collision-avoidance via prefix/suffix vars.

Module tiers (recommended):
1) primitives/low-level (stable, long-lived): vpc-core, iam-roles, iam-policies, kms, dns-zone, network-acls. These expose narrow, mostly stable outputs.
2) infra-operators (composed primitives): eks-cluster-core, eks-node-pool, gke-cluster-core. These accept primitives as inputs (vpc id/subnets, iam role ARNs).
3) stacks/environment (opinionated assembly): redwood-private-env (glues primitives + infra-operators with company defaults, testing hooks).

Naming & versioning conventions:
- Module names: short, hyphenated, explicit (vpc-core, iam-role-standard, eks-cluster-core).
- Releases: semantic versioning for module registry. Use MAJOR bump when outputs/inputs break.
- Changelog in module root: README includes upgrade notes and common gotchas.

Input conventions (examples & rationale):
- Always allow externally-provided IDs for upstream resources: e.g., vpc_core should accept optional vpc_id and subnets map. This supports migration-from-manual-to-module.
- Keep booleans for feature gates (eg enable_flow_logs) and avoid complex nested maps unless necessary.
- Provide both computed and overridable outputs: allow users to supply custom_kms_key or have module create one.

Example variables (vpc-core):
- variable "name_prefix" { type = string }
- variable "cidr_block" { type = string }
- variable "private_subnet_cidrs" { type = list(string) }
- variable "public_subnet_cidrs" { type = list(string) }
- variable "enable_flow_logs" { type = bool, default = false }
- variable "aws_tags" { type = map(string), default = {} }

Example outputs (vpc-core):
- output "vpc_id" { value = aws_vpc.main.id }
- output "private_subnet_ids" { value = aws_subnet.private.*.id }
- output "public_subnet_ids" { value = aws_subnet.public.*.id }
- output "routes" { value = aws_route_table.private.*.id }
Notes: Keep outputs typed and stable. Avoid collateral outputs (internal ARNs) unless consumers need them.

IAM module patterns:
- Keep small role modules: iam-role-basic (trust policy template + attachable policy ARNs). Complex managed policies should live in iam-policies module.
- Expose role_arn and role_name as outputs. If role contains inline policy, its version should be tracked in module versioning.
- For cross-account roles, explicit variables for external_account_ids and condition blocks.

Kubernetes cluster modules (eks-cluster-core):
- Inputs: cluster_name, vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, public_subnet_ids, cluster_version (default pinned), service_role_arn (optional).
- Outputs: cluster_endpoint, cluster_ca_cert, cluster_security_group_id, kubeconfig (sensitive; prefer writing to SSM or file in CI).
- Node pools should be distinct modules (eks-node-pool) with clear inputs: cluster_id, instance_type, asg_min/max, taints/labels.
- Avoid embedding node pools inside cluster core to allow mixed nodes (spot + on-demand).

Outputs as stable contracts:
- Treat outputs like API endpoints. If a module used in many places exposes output X, be conservative about changing X.
- Add new outputs instead of renaming. If renaming is unavoidable, deprecate with a warning in README and bump MAJOR.

Upgrade and migration playbook (high level):
1) Add new outputs/inputs in a backward-compatible way (non-breaking).
2) Update consumers to adopt new outputs (can be done in separate PRs).
3) After consumers are migrated, remove old/compat outputs in a major release.
4) For input changes that are breaking, provide a migration script/notes and a conversion plan (example: migrating from single-subnet to multi-az subnets).

Example migration note (single -> multi AZ for VPC):
- Step A: Module v1.1 adds optional multi_az_subnets variable; if not provided, module computes single AZ layout to preserve behavior.
- Step B: Consumers adopt new var and pass lists.
- Step C: Once all consumers pass lists, v2.0 drops single-AZ fallback and enforces lists.

Testing and CI rules:
- Each module must include: unit-style tests (terraform validate + tflint), small integration plan runs in ephemeral accounts (terraform plan only) in CI.
- Smoke apply in a sandbox account (nightly) for critical primitives: vpc-core, eks-cluster-core. Use ephemeral naming and tear down.
- Add regression guardrails: a GH action that flags if outputs are removed or types changed. Diff outputs.json from previous release and fail PR if outputs deleted without MAJOR bump.

Safety & runtime considerations:
- Avoid provisioning very large resource lists during plan (e.g., thousands of subnets). Where necessary, provide opt-in pagination or external data sources.
- Tagging: modules should accept a tags map and merge with internal tags. Do not hardcode org tags.

Inter-module contract examples (what to pass):
- eks-cluster-core -> expects vpc module outputs: { vpc_id, private_subnet_ids, public_subnet_ids }
- eks-node-pool -> expects cluster_output: { cluster_id, cluster_endpoint, cluster_ca_cert } and iam-role-arn for node role

Acceptance criteria for new modules or major changes:
- README with inputs/outputs lists, sample usage, and upgrade notes.
- Automated tests in CI that run plan at minimum.
- At least one integration test in sandbox for primitives.
- Module registry package (if used) has semantic version and changelog.

Checklist for reviewers (quick):
- Does module have a single clear responsibility?
- Are inputs minimal and explicit? No hidden lookups?
- Are outputs necessary and named clearly?
- Is there a documented migration/upgrade path?
- CI checks present: validate, fmt, tflint, plan test?
- README contains example usage and typical values.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Standardize names for subnet outputs across clouds (aws: private_subnet_ids vs gcp: private_subnet_self_links). Do we normalize consumer input shape in a shim module? (ACTION: discuss with multi-cloud team)
- How do we best store sensitive outputs (kubeconfig)? SSM Parameter Store vs local artifacts for CI? (Security should weigh in)
- Policy for removing deprecated outputs: default deprecation window = 90 days? 6 months? (Proposal: 3 months for infra-team-only primitives, 6 months for cross-team).

Small reference snippets (do not copy blindly):
- Stable output example: output "database_subnet_ids" { description = "Private subnet IDs for DB tier" value = aws_subnet.db.*.id }
- Deprecation note in README: "v1.0 -> v2.0: output 'subnet_ids' renamed to 'private_subnet_ids'. Consumers should migrate by 2024-06-01."

Author notes and quick wins:
- Add GH Action to compute outputs drift between branches and post a comment with diff summary.
- Publish a short training session for infra engineers on module boundaries and upgrade lifecycle.

Appendix: minimal example usage (vpc + eks combo)
- module "vpc" { source = "git::ssh://.../modules/vpc-core.git" name_prefix = "redwood-prod" cidr_block = "10.0.0.0/16" }
- module "eks" { source = "git::ssh://.../modules/eks-cluster-core.git" vpc_id = module.vpc.vpc_id private_subnet_ids = module.vpc.private_subnet_ids }

If you take one thing away: treat module outputs as public contracts. Add before you remove, and version strictly.

Notes to reviewers: this is intentionally terse — expand the examples that match your cloud provider and product needs. Follow-ups: create cloud-specific appendix (aws/gcp/az) and build the GH outputs-diff action (JIRA-OPS-987).

Last edited by Aisha — feel free to leave review comments inline or add to linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infrastructure/pull/412
